130	    """One container holding a clone of the repo; the project lives in `subdir` of the clone."""
131	
132	    def __init__(self, container, role, image, subdir="", deadline=None):
133	        self.container, self.role, self.image, self.subdir = container, role, image, subdir
134	        self.deadline = deadline
135	        self.home = NODE_HOME if image.startswith("node:") else OTHER_HOME
136	        self.image_major = int(image[5:].split("-")[0]) if image.startswith("node:") else None
137	        self.steps = []
138	        self.pm = self.install_dir = None
139	        self.has_build = False
140	        self.frozen = True        # False once a lockfile was removed to be regenerated
141	        self.versions = ""
142	        self.last_out = ""
143	        self.touched = []         # repo-relative paths the agent wrote or removed
144	        self.cloned = False
145	        self.ptype, self.why, self.cap_s = "unsupported", "", 900
146	        self.forge = False        # the repo has a foundry.toml, so forge is installed
147	        self.env_example = ""
148	        self.gaps = []            # reasons a passing run still has gaps
149	        self.proof = {}           # how the serve step passed: "http" (GET /) or "service" (alive)
150	        self.accept_gap = None    # (step, reason) the model named as an external need; that step
151	                                  # failing then counts as a gap, here and in the verifier
152	
153	    @property
154	    def proj(self):
155	        return f"repo/{self.subdir}" if self.subdir else "repo"
156	
157	    def rel(self, name):
158	        return f"{self.subdir}/{name}" if self.subdir else name
159	
160	    def raw(self, cmd, data=None, timeout=120):
161	        return exec_raw(self.container, cmd, data, timeout, self.home)
162	
163	    def sh(self, name, cmd, user="1000:1000"):
164	        timeout = self.cap_s
165	        if self.deadline:
166	            timeout = int(max(30, min(timeout, self.deadline - time.monotonic())))
167	        with tool_span(f"{self.role}.{name}") as sp:
168	            rec, out = step(name, self.container, cmd, timeout, self.home, user)
169	            self.steps.append(rec)
170	            tail = "\n".join(rec["output_tail"])
171	            sp.set_attribute("neatlogs.tool.name", f"{self.role}.{name}")
172	            sp.set_attribute("command", cmd)
173	            sp.set_attribute("exit_code", rec["exit_code"])
174	            sp.set_attribute("duration_s", rec["duration_s"])
175	            sp.set_attribute("output_tail", tail)
176	            if rec["exit_code"]:
177	                sp.set_attribute("neatlogs.tool.is_error", True)
178	                sp.set_attribute("error", tail.splitlines()[-1] if tail else f"exit {rec['exit_code']}")
179	        self.last_out = out
180	        return rec["exit_code"] == 0
181	
182	    def read(self, path):
183	        code, out, _ = self.raw(f"cat {shlex.quote('repo/' + path)}")
184	        return out if code == 0 else None
185	
186	    def read_many(self, paths):
187	        """{path: content} for the repo-relative paths that exist, in one container call."""
188	        quoted = " ".join(shlex.quote(p) for p in paths)
189	        script = (f'cd repo && for f in {quoted}; do [ -f "$f" ] && '
190	                  f'{{ printf "\\0FILE %s\\0" "$f"; cat "$f"; }}; done; true')
191	        _, out, _ = self.raw(script)
192	        files = {}
193	        for chunk in out.split("\0FILE ")[1:]:
194	            path, _, text = chunk.partition("\0")
195	            files[path] = text
196	        return files
197	
198	    def write(self, files):
199	        for path, content in files.items():
200	            q = shlex.quote("repo/" + path)
201	            code, _, err = self.raw(f"mkdir -p \"$(dirname {q})\" && cat > {q}", content)
202	            if code:
203	                raise RuntimeError(f"write {path} failed: {err.strip()}")
204	            self.touched.append(path)
205	        return list(files)
206	
207	    def remove(self, paths):
208	        for path in paths:
209	            self.raw(f"rm -f {shlex.quote('repo/' + path)}")
210	            self.touched.append(path)
211	            self.frozen = False
212	        return paths
213	
214	    def rule_files(self):
215	        """Contents of the files the rules read: project dir first, repo root as fallback
216	        (never for package.json)."""
217	        files, self.where = {}, {}
218	        found = self.read_many([p for n in RULE_FILES for p in {self.rel(n), n}])
219	        for name in RULE_FILES:
220	            for path in dict.fromkeys([self.rel(name), name]):
221	                if path in found:
222	                    files[name], self.where[name] = found[path], path
223	                    break
224	                if name == "package.json":
225	                    break
226	        return files
227	
228	    def clone(self, repo, sha):
229	        check = f" && test -d {shlex.quote(self.subdir)}" if self.subdir else ""
230	        self.cloned = self.sh("clone", f"git clone -q https://github.com/{repo}.git repo && cd repo "
231	                                       f"&& git checkout -q {sha}{check}")
232	        return self.cloned
233	
234	    def classify(self):
235	        """Detect the project type from the manifests, and whether forge is needed.
236	        Returns the manifest contents."""
237	        found = self.read_many([self.rel(n) for n in MANIFESTS])
238	        files = {n: found[self.rel(n)] for n in MANIFESTS if self.rel(n) in found}
239	        _, out, _ = self.raw(f"cd {shlex.quote(self.proj)} && git ls-files -- '*package.json' "
240	                             "'*foundry.toml' | head -80")
241	        names = out.split()
242	        self.forge = any(n.endswith("foundry.toml") for n in names)
243	        members = {}
244	        if "pnpm-workspace.yaml" in files or '"workspaces"' in files.get("package.json", ""):
245	            paths = [self.rel(n) for n in names if n.endswith("package.json")]
246	            members = self.read_many(paths)
247	        self.ptype, self.why = detect_type(files, members)
248	        self.forge = self.forge or self.ptype == "foundry"
249	        self.cap_s = CAP_MINUTES[family(self.ptype)] * 60
250	        self.env_example = files.get(".env.example", "")
251	        return files
252	
253	    def target_image(self, files):
254	        """The toolchain image the project type needs."""
255	        if family(self.ptype) == "rust":
256	            tag, why = rust_version(files)
257	            self.why += f"; {why}"
258	            return f"rust:{tag}-bookworm"
259	        return f"node:{node_major(files)[0] or BASELINE_NODE}-bookworm"

261	    def apply_patch(self, patch):
262	        code, _, err = self.raw("cd repo && git apply --whitespace=nowarn -", patch)

266	    def diff(self):
267	        """Patch of the files the agent touched, new files included."""
268	        paths = " ".join(shlex.quote(p) for p in dict.fromkeys(self.touched))
269	        if not paths:
270	            return ""
271	        _, out, _ = self.raw(f"cd repo && git add -N -- {paths} 2>/dev/null; "
272	                             f"git diff --no-color --no-ext-diff -- {paths}")
273	        return out

275	    def prune(self, attempts):
276	        """After a pass with several applied attempts: revert the files only the attempts that did
277	        not pass touched, re-run once, and keep the smaller patch only if it passes. Returns
278	        {"files": [...], "kept": bool}, or None when there is nothing to prune."""
279	        applied = [a for a in attempts if a.get("status") == "applied"]
280	        if len(applied) < 2 or (self.deadline and time.monotonic() > self.deadline):
281	            return None
282	        keep = set(applied[-1]["files"])
283	        stale = list(dict.fromkeys(p for a in applied[:-1] for p in a["files"] if p not in keep))
284	        if not stale:
285	            return None
286	        before = self.read_many(stale)           # a path missing here was removed by the agent
287	        state = (self.frozen, self.gaps, self.proof)
288	        for path in stale:                       # tracked files back from git, new files deleted
289	            q = shlex.quote(path)
290	            self.raw(f"cd repo && (git checkout -q -- {q} 2>/dev/null || rm -f {q})")
291	        self.frozen = True                       # the verifier starts from the original lockfile
292	        kept = self.pipeline() is None
293	        if not kept:
294	            self.frozen, self.gaps, self.proof = state
295	            self.write(before)
296	            self.remove([p for p in stale if p not in before])
297	            self.frozen = state[0]
298	        return {"files": stale, "kept": kept}

300	    def toolchain_cmd(self, files):
301	        """Rust: the image's toolchain as it is. Otherwise the Node major from .nvmrc (the image's
302	        by default) and an npm pin, with pnpm and yarn from corepack; plus a pinned Foundry
303	        release (and submodules) when the repo has a foundry.toml."""
304	        if family(self.ptype) == "rust":
305	            return f"cd {self.proj} && rustc --version && cargo --version"
306	        major = parse_major(files.get(".nvmrc")) or self.image_major
307	        cmd = "mkdir -p $HOME/.local/bin && corepack enable --install-directory $HOME/.local/bin"
308	        cmd += (f" && npm install --prefix $HOME/.node node@{major}" if major != self.image_major
309	                else " && rm -rf $HOME/.node")
310	        try:
311	            declared = json.loads(files.get("package.json") or "{}").get("packageManager", "")
312	        except ValueError:
313	            declared = ""
314	        pins = []                 # pinned into $HOME/.pm, which is on PATH (see ENV_PREFIX)
315	        if declared.startswith("npm@"):
316	            pins.append(f"npm@{declared[4:].split('+')[0]}")
317	        bun = bun_version(files)
318	        if bun:
319	            pins.append(f"bun@{bun}")
320	        cmd += (f" && npm install --prefix $HOME/.pm {' '.join(pins)}" if pins
321	                else " && rm -rf $HOME/.pm")
322	        if bun:
323	            cmd += " && bun --version"
324	        if self.forge:
325	            url = ("https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry/releases/download/"
326	                   f"{FOUNDRY_RELEASE}/foundry_{FOUNDRY_RELEASE}_linux_$(dpkg --print-architecture).tar.gz")
327	            cmd += (f" && mkdir -p $HOME/.foundry/bin && curl -fsSL {url} | tar -xz -C $HOME/.foundry/bin"
328	                    " && (cd repo && git submodule update --init --recursive -q) && forge --version")
329	        return cmd + " && node --version"

331	    def detect(self, files):
332	        """Package manager from the lockfile; without one, the packageManager field or npm, with
333	        a non-frozen install."""
334	        found = detect_pm(files)
335	        self.steps.append({"name": "detect", "command": "lockfile", "exit_code": 0, "duration_s": 0,
336	                           "package_manager": found, "output_tail": [] if found else
337	                           ["no lockfile; using the packageManager field or npm"]})
338	        try:
339	            pkg = json.loads(files.get("package.json") or "{}")
340	        except ValueError:
341	            pkg = {}
342	        self.has_build = "build" in (pkg.get("scripts") or {})
343	        lock = next((n for n, pm in LOCKFILES if pm == found and n in files), None)
344	        if not lock:      # no lockfile for the detected manager (Bun by packageManager field only)
345	            declared = str(pkg.get("packageManager", "")).split("@")[0]
346	            self.pm = found or (declared if declared in ("pnpm", "yarn") else "npm")

366	        """Start the app, wait for a new port, GET /, stop the server (probe.js does the check)."""
367	        s = scripts(files)
368	        start = (f"{pm} run dev" if "dev" in s and "start" not in s

377	        """The (step, command) list the proof bar of this project type requires."""
378	        p, t = self.proj, self.ptype
379	        if t == "rust":

381	        if self.pm is None and (t != "foundry" or detect_pm(files)):

388	        if t == "foundry":

390	        if self.has_build:

402	    def failed(self, name):
403	        """The failure record for the step that just ran, or None when it only fails because a
404	        secret or external service is needed (recorded as a gap, the run stops there)."""
405	        rec = self.steps[-1]
406	        secret = needs_secret(self.last_out, self.env_example) if name != "toolchain" else None
407	        if secret:
408	            self.gaps.append(f"needs {secret} ({name} step)")
409	            return None
410	        if self.accept_gap and name == self.accept_gap[0]:
411	            self.gaps.append(f"needs {self.accept_gap[1]} ({name} step)")
412	            return None
413	        return {"step": name, "command": rec["command"], "exit_code": rec["exit_code"]}

415	    def pipeline(self):
416	        """toolchain, .env, then the steps of the project type. Returns None when every step
417	        passed or a secret gap ended the run (see self.gaps), else {step, command, exit_code}."""
418	        self.gaps, self.proof = [], {}
419	        files = self.rule_files()
420	        pin = rustup_install(files) if family(self.ptype) == "rust" else ""
421	        if pin and not self.sh("toolchain-pin", pin, user="0:0"):   # root, before the user steps
422	            return self.failed("toolchain")
423	        if not self.sh("toolchain", self.toolchain_cmd(files)):
424	            return self.failed("toolchain")
425	        lines = [l for l in self.last_out.strip().splitlines() if l.strip()]
426	        self.versions = ", ".join(lines[-2:]) if self.forge or family(self.ptype) == "rust" \
427	            else (f"node {lines[-1]}" if lines else "")
428	        self.fill_env()

433	                return self.failed(name)
434	            if name == "serve":

# neatHack build log

## Project
**Resurgo** keeps a builder's projects runnable: it fresh-clones each repo, repairs what rotted, and proves the fix in a clean container before opening a pull request.

## Team
Timidan (solo, with coding agents).

## Stack
- Agent: Python, LangGraph, FastAPI.
- Web: React, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, SmoothUI.
- Runs: Docker containers on a self-hosted server, one build at a time with resource caps.
- Model: an OpenAI model through a self-hosted Hermes gateway.
- neatlogs: traces every run; before/after comparison of agent versions.
- Entire: checkpoints on every agent-made commit; entire-graph maps each repo during runs.
- cfo.ai: business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway).
- Dodo Payments: test-mode checkout for prepaid fix credits.

## Build log
### 10 Oct 2026
- Created the repository. Enabled Entire for Claude Code and Codex, installed entire-graph, and turned on secret, email, phone and IP redaction for checkpoints.

- Milestone 1, the thin path: `uv run python -m resurgo.run <owner/repo> <sha>` starts a capped `node:24-bookworm` container, clones the repo at the SHA, detects the package manager from the lockfile, enables corepack and runs the install. It then repeats the same steps in a second fresh "verifier" container, writes `runs/<run-id>/result.json`, and removes both containers.
- What works: clone, lockfile detection, corepack, the install step, both containers, the JSON record, and cleanup (no containers left after the run). One bug found on the way: corepack failed first because `~/.local/bin` did not exist in the image; fixed with `mkdir -p`.
- First real run, Timidan/rinne at 5c3370f9a736: `result=fail`. Both containers cloned, detected pnpm and enabled corepack, then `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exited 1 in 26.6s (agent) and 19.5s (verifier) with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS: Ignored build scripts: esbuild@0.25.12` (pnpm 12.10.1). This is the failure the plan expected, and the verifier reproduced it. Summary line: `20261010T091116Z-5c3370f Timidan/rinne@5c3370f9a736 result=fail agent=fail verifier=fail 119s agent:install exit 1`.
- Not verified: the neatlogs trace. `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` is not set in `.env`, so the run printed a warning and skipped tracing. The tracing code is written but has never sent a span.
- Neatlogs tracing, done properly. The old code made spans with `opentelemetry.trace.get_tracer()`, but `neatlogs.init()` uses its own provider, so nothing reached Neatlogs. Replaced it with the SDK's live `neatlogs.trace()` spans: one `WORKFLOW` span per run (repo, sha, agent_version, result) and one `TOOL` span per container step (command, exit code, duration, scrubbed output tail, error). `init()` runs once after `.env` loads, `flush()` and `shutdown()` run in `finally`, and a missing key warns and runs untraced. Installed `neatlogs[langchain]` for the LangGraph step.
- Delivery check: `neatlogs doctor --probe` passes, including TRACE_VISIBLE and TRACE_FINALIZED. The Timidan/rinne run at 5c3370f9a736 gave the same `result=fail` (pnpm install exit 1) in 133s. I did not open the run's trace in the Neatlogs UI, so its span tree is unchecked.
- LangGraph tracing rules are in `docs/NEATLOGS.md`. The skills repo has no `skill-menu.json`; the rules come from its Python framework reference.

- Milestone 2a, the agent loop for Node projects. `--path <subdir>` runs a project inside a repo. When install or build fails, a LangGraph loop runs: deterministic rules first (Node major from `engines.node`, `.nvmrc`, `.node-version` or volta; package manager from the `packageManager` field or the lockfile format; each is written as a file fix), then diagnose, propose strict JSON, apply config fixes in the container, and rerun. Budget: 4 fix attempts (a rule candidate counts as one) and 15 minutes. Code fixes are recorded as `needs_approval`, never applied. Invalid JSON is re-asked once and recorded as recovery. The model gateway is wrapped as a LangChain chat model so neatlogs records each call; token counts are estimates (characters / 4) and labelled so. A run is `fixed` only if a fresh container, applying only `fix.patch` to a clean clone, passes install and build.
- Real runs, one each. Timidan/rinne at 5c3370f9a736: `fixed`, 3 model calls, 694s. The model first set `pnpm.onlyBuiltDependencies` in package.json, then moved it to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, then used `allowBuilds` (pnpm 12 no longer reads the older settings). Install passed on the third fix and the verifier passed. The patch still contains the two earlier, ineffective edits. Timidan/agent-arena at f6fc3243ac98 with `--path commentator`: `fixed`, 1 model call, 570s. Install failed compiling better-sqlite3 against Node 24 (277s); the model wrote `commentator/.nvmrc` with `20`; install and build then passed in the agent and in the verifier. No rule fired in either run.

- Not verified: the neatlogs trace hierarchy (LLM and CHAIN spans under the WORKFLOW span) was not opened in the UI. The runs sent spans, but I did not check them.

A record in `runs/` for the same repo, SHA, path and agent version is reused. PRs open only with `RESURGO_AUTO_PR=1`, for a passed run with a `fix.patch` that needs no approval. Finished installations are re-queued after 7 days. Checked with a fake GitHub in `resurgo/test_worker.py`; not run against the real App from this machine.

  - Weakening guard: before a proposal is applied it is rejected if it adds or changes a `foundry.toml` test filter (`match_*` / `no_match_*`), deletes more test files than it writes (a rename is a deletion plus a written test file, so it passes), or changes the `test` script of a package.json. The model gets one re-ask with "this skips or weakens tests"; a second weakening ends the run as `broken` with the reason in `detail`, and the rejected proposal is kept in `attempts` with status `rejected`.
  - Gap answer: `{"kind": "gap", "reason": ...}` is accepted only when the failing step is test or serve (install and build ran before it and passed); otherwise it is re-asked like any rejected reply. An accepted gap changes nothing: the run goes to the verifier with `Box.accept_gap` set, so that step failing counts as `needs <reason> (<step> step)` in `gaps` and the result is `runs_with_gaps`, the same path as a missing secret. ## Demo
Not available yet.

## Known limitations and next steps
- Foundry and Rust each have one real run that passed without a fix; the repair loop has not run on either.
- A `start` script that opens no port passes as a "service" after 30 seconds alive, which is a weaker proof than GET /; a web app that takes longer than 30 seconds to open its port would be recorded as a service.
- Monorepos get the library proof bar (install, build, test); their apps are not started.
- The patch is cumulative unless pruning (v2) applies: it only reverts files that failed attempts alone touched, and it has not run in a container yet.
- Bun support has never run on a real repo.
- A rule that fires after a late test failure re-runs install and build, which can spend the whole budget before the model sees the failure (sentry-somnia).
- Reruns always start from install. Lockfile regeneration (an empty-content lockfile entry) and npm pins are implemented but have not been exercised on a real repo.
- The 25-minute Node budget covers the fix loop, not the verifier. Many per-file `docker exec` calls on the remote host made runs slow before reads were batched.
- The `resurgo-runs` network is created if missing and left in place after runs.

def test_fill_env_regenerates_runner_env_but_keeps_committed(tmp_path):
    import subprocess
    from resurgo import run as runner

    def box_in(name, files):
        root = tmp_path / name
        (root / "repo").mkdir(parents=True)
        for fname, text in files.items():
            (root / "repo" / fname).write_text(text)
        git = ["git", "-C", str(root / "repo"), "-c", "user.name=t", "-c", "user.email=t@t"]
        for args in (["init", "-q"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-qm", "x"]):
            subprocess.run(git + args, check=True)

        def raw(cmd, data=None, timeout=120):
            p = subprocess.run(["bash", "-c", cmd], input=data or "", capture_output=True, text=True,
                               cwd=root)
            return p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr
        box = runner.Box("c", "agent", "node:24-bookworm")
        box.raw = raw
        return box, root / "repo"

    box, repo = box_in("made", {".env.example": "DB=/var/lib/x/db.sqlite\n"})
    box.fill_env()
    assert "/var/lib/x" in (repo / ".env").read_text()
    (repo / ".env.example").write_text("DB=./db.sqlite\n")
    box.fill_env()
    assert "./db.sqlite" in (repo / ".env").read_text()

    box, repo = box_in("committed", {".env.example": "A=1\n", ".env": "A=committed\n"})
    box.fill_env()
    assert (repo / ".env").read_text() == "A=committed\n"

- Agent v2.2 (`__version__` 0.2.2), one runner fix. In the v2.1 agent-arena run the model's fourth attempt correctly changed `CHECKPOINT_DB` in `.env.example` to a relative path, but `fill_env` wrote `.env` only if it did not exist, and the runner had already written it on the first pipeline run, so the edit never reached the server. `fill_env` now rewrites `.env` from the current `.env.example` on every pipeline run, unless the repo tracks `.env` at the run's commit (`git ls-files --error-unmatch`). Dummy values are unchanged. The verifier gets the same behaviour because it writes `.env` in its fresh clone after the patch is applied. Test: `test_fill_env_regenerates_runner_env_but_keeps_committed` runs the real shell command against a temp git repo; `uv run --with pytest pytest -q resurgo`: 13 passed.
- v2.2 real run, Timidan/agent-arena at f6fc3243ac98 `--path commentator` (tag `v2.2`, set `dev`, nothing tuned): `runs`, 1987s, 1 model call. The native-module rule wrote `.nvmrc` 22; the first serve failed on the missing sqlite directory; the model then changed `.env.example` to `CHECKPOINT_DB=./checkpoint.sqlite` (a config fix, no approval needed), serve passed on the re-run, and the verifier passed install, build and serve from `fix.patch` (`.env.example` and `.nvmrc`). Caveats: serve passes as a "service" (the bot opens no port and stays alive 30 seconds), which is the weaker proof, and the dummy `APP_HEX` means this does not show the bot works against a real chain. Not a v2.2 regression, but seen here: pruning reverted `.nvmrc` (only the rule attempt touched it, and the model's attempt did not), the re-run failed install on Node 24 (289s), and the prune was discarded (`kept: false`); the stale-file test treats a file an earlier passing step depended on as removable.

content.text:
The fix is committed as `f1c3e9b`, nothing is pushed, and the `Timidan/agent-arena` v2.2 dev run ended `runs`.

**Fix**
- `Box.fill_env` in `resurgo/run.py` now rewrites `.env` from the current `.env.example` on every pipeline run. It skips the write only when the repo tracks `.env` at the run's commit.
- Dummy values are unchanged, and the verifier takes the same path on its fresh clone.
- I added one test, `test_fill_env_regenerates_runner_env_but_keeps_committed`. `uv run --with pytest pytest -q resurgo` gives 13 passed.
- I bumped `__version__` to 0.2.2. You didn't ask for this; I did it so the install worker doesn't reuse v2.1 records.

**Run** (`f6fc3243ac98`, `--path commentator`, tag `v2.2`, set `dev`, 1987s, 1 model call)
- The native-module rule wrote `.nvmrc` 22 and install and build passed. The first serve failed on the missing sqlite directory.
- The model then changed `CHECKPOINT_DB` in `.env.example` to `./checkpoint.sqlite`. This is a config fix, so no approval is needed. Serve passed on the re-run, which the old `fill_env` would have blocked.
- The verifier passed install, build and serve from `fix.patch` (`.env.example` plus `.nvmrc`).

**Caveats**
- Serve passes only as a "service": the bot opens no port and stays alive for 30 seconds. It runs with a dummy `APP_HEX`, so this doesn't show the bot works against a real chain.
- Pruning reverted `.nvmrc` because only the rule attempt touched it. The re-run then failed install on Node 24 (289s) and the prune was discarded (`kept: false`). This is existing behaviour, not caused by this change, and I left it alone because it was out of scope. It wastes one install and could cost a repo its budget, so it is worth a fix before the held-out sweep.

The `hackathon.md` entry records the above, and the commit carries no attribution trailer, per your CLAUDE.md.
